newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's peso dives 8.3 vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's peso dives 8.3 vs dollar.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed 8.3 pesos down against the dollar at 1,065 as industry scrambled to service foreign debts in anticipation of even bigger falls, interbank dealers said.
The peso has fallen 24.5 pesos against the dollar this week so far.

Dealers said certain sectors were holding back their dollar export earnings, waiting for the peso rate to drop further in the coming days. This, they said, had led to a shortage of greenbacks in the market.
Industry, meanwhile, continued its wave of panic buying to service foreign debts in advance of what they expect will be an even greater devaluation in the Colombian currency.
Dealers reported 411 operations worth a total $174 million. The peso opened at an intraday low of 1,052 and closed at the high.
They say the peso is likely to stay at around the same rate until at least the end of the week as businesses balance their books for month end.

Dealers declined to speculate on prospects for February, citing numerous factors of potential market uncertainty including the effects of the recently-declared state of economic emergency and the forthcoming U.S. decision on whether to exclude Colombia from its list of allies in the drug war -- so-called decertification -- for the second consecutive year.
